title: Why the Cold War Ended
objective: After this level you can weigh the explanations for the Cold War's end in 1989 to 1991, from American pressure under Reagan to Gorbachev's reforms and the Soviet economy.
summary: Gorbachev needed to cut military spending; Poland led 1989’s revolutions; the Soviet Union ended in 1991. Historians weigh pressure, protest, reform and economics.

cards.headline: In 1989 the Berlin Wall fell. By the end of 1991 the Soviet Union was gone.
cards.body: Who deserves the credit? Americans, Soviets and Eastern Europeans all tell the story differently, and historians still weigh it.

cards.headline: A new Soviet leader
cards.body: Mikhail Gorbachev became the Soviet leader in March 1985 and inherited a stagnant economy. To restructure it, he needed to reduce military spending at home and political tensions abroad. He and President Ronald Reagan met in four summits between 1985 and 1988. In December 1987 they signed the INF Treaty, which eliminated an entire class of missiles.

cards.headline: The wall comes down
cards.body: Gorbachev loosened Soviet control of Eastern Europe, and people there moved fast. The first revolution of 1989 came in Poland, where the Solidarity movement won freer elections. In November 1989 the Berlin Wall came down, and Communist rule fell across Eastern Europe. On December 25, 1991, Gorbachev resigned and the Soviet flag was lowered over the Kremlin for the last time.

cards.headline: Three kinds of explanation
cards.body: Historians offer rival explanations. Some credit American pressure: Reagan’s military buildup and his Strategic Defense Initiative. Others stress the people of Eastern Europe, especially in Poland, and Soviet overreach in the war in Afghanistan. Still others point to the implosion of the Soviet economy. Each explanation fits some of the evidence.

cards.headline: Weighing them
cards.body: Historians have reached no consensus on how much weight each factor deserves. The State Department’s own historians write that Gorbachev took the initiative in arms control, and that Reagan was well prepared to negotiate. So ask how the causes interact: would pressure have worked without a Soviet leader ready to respond? Would reform have gone so far without people in the streets?

cards.headline: Why the Cold War Ended: explained
learned: Gorbachev needed to cut military spending to fix the economy
Poland led 1989; the Soviet Union ended in December 1991
Historians have reached no consensus on the weights

questions.prompt: Put these steps in the end of the Cold War in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Gorbachev became the Soviet leader in 1985 and signed the INF Treaty in 1987. Solidarity won freer elections in Poland in 1989, the Berlin Wall came down that November, and Gorbachev resigned on December 25, 1991.

questions.prompt: A student says the Cold War ended only because of Reagan’s military buildup. Which fact most complicates that single-cause story?

options.label: Reagan launched a large military buildup
options.rationale: That supports the student’s story rather than complicating it.

options.label: Poland’s Solidarity movement led the first revolution of 1989
The Soviet flag came down in 1991
options.rationale: That is the outcome, not a cause.

options.label: The Berlin Wall had divided the city
options.rationale: That describes the division, not why it ended.

questions.explanation: Eastern Europeans, starting with Poland’s Solidarity, drove the revolutions of 1989: evidence for a cause beyond American pressure.

questions.prompt: The State Department’s historians call French help crucial to the win at Yorktown (Level 26). What do they say about Gorbachev and arms control?

options.label: Gorbachev took the initiative, and Reagan was well prepared to negotiate
Reagan forced Gorbachev to sign against his will
options.rationale: They credit Gorbachev with taking the initiative.

options.label: Gorbachev refused every treaty Reagan proposed
options.rationale: They signed the INF Treaty in 1987.

options.label: Neither leader played any real role
options.rationale: They held four summits and signed a treaty.

questions.explanation: As with Yorktown, the outcome depended on more than one side: Gorbachev took the initiative and Reagan was ready to negotiate.
